ac: a — 'and' before a vowel (ac ef); also the preposition a 'with' before a vowel (ymgael ac ef 'meet with him', ymordiwes ac ef) · the manuscript also writes ac before some consonants (Ac wal, Ac val, ac racdaw) · also 'as' after an equative or kymeint (kymeint ac ynot ti 'as much as in you'; mor anwedus ac ar y wnaethoed 'as unseemly as what she had done')
yna: yna (yna) — then; adverb (Yna y rodes Arawn y furuf)
guedy: guedy (gwedi) — after; preposition (A guedy y medwl hwnnw 'and after that thought')
daruot: daruot (darfod) — to finish, be finished, happen; verbal noun, with y/i of the person (kynn daruot idaw ymgueiraw 'before he had finished making ready')
y: y — (1) the article 'the' (y llys); (2) 'his, her, its' (y uryt: soft mutation = his; y hymdidan: h-prefix = her); (3) 'to' (y hela, y gyuoeth); (4) preverbal particle after a fronted adverb or object (yno y bu, Pwyll... a oed); (5) the relative in oblique relations (o'r a welsei) · (6) 'from' in y gan, y wrth 'from, compared with' (y gan y uarch 'from his horse'; y wrth y ffryt hi 'compared with her form'); (7) infixed object 'him, her, it' after a (a'y guelei 'who saw her'); (8) in a'y kymriw it is the second letter of ae 'either' (see a) · also (9) y am, y amdanaw 'from about, off' (y amdanaw 'off him'); y am hynny 'around that, beyond that, besides' · also (10) 'their' (for eu), with no mutation (y bot 'their being'; y kymryt 'their taking' = to take them) · also (11) 'in' (y'th wlat ti 'in your country') · (12) the particle y before mae introducing a reported fact (y may brawt … a wnaeth hynny 'that it is a brother who did that')
tangneued: tangneued (tangnefedd) — peace; noun f. (ef a barei tangneued 'he would make peace'); no mutation (object, radical)
o: o (o) — (1) 'of, from' preposition; (2) 'if' before a verb (o gwneuthum gam 'if I did wrong') · also 'on, by' (o pedestric 'on foot'), 'out of, from' (o'th garyat ti 'from love of you'), 'of' a kind (pryt … o uorwyn 'the looks of (any) maiden') · also agent after a verbal noun, 'by' (troi o Pwyll y got 'Pwyll turning the bag'); o gosp 'of punishment'
uendigeiduran: Proper name — Bendigeidfran; spelling with -d; soft-mutated (b>u) after the preposition wrth 'to' (wrth Uendigeiduran 'to Bendigeidfran') · also soft as object of a finite verb (y cauas Uendigeiduran 'where he found Bendigeidfran')
mab: mab (mab) — son, boy; noun m. (mab a anet idaw 'a son was born to him'); no mutation (subject, fronted)
attaw: at — conjugated preposition 'to him' (y marchawc a doeth attaw 'the horseman came to him')
gan: gan (gan) — with, by; preposition, softening the next word; possession is 'with' a person or thing (oed gan y march 'the horse had', literally 'was with the horse'); y gan 'from' (y gan y uarch 'from his horse'); base of gennyf, ganthaw, genthi etc. · also 'from', without y (ny chaffei namyn yr un atteb gan y gwraged 'she would get only the same answer from the women'; yny gigleu gan lawer 'until he heard from many')
at: at — preposition 'to, towards' (at y cwn 'to the dogs')
uanawydan: Proper name — Manawydan; soft-mutated (m>u) as a person addressed, vocative (Kyuodwch, Uanawydan uab Llyr 'rise, Manawydan son of Llŷr')
a: a — (1) preverbal/relative particle before a verb, causes soft mutation (Pwyll … a oed; ef a welei); (2) 'and' before a consonant, spirant mutation (a chanu, a fob); (3) 'with' (a'y gydymdeithon; gyt a thi); (4) vocative particle (A unben); (5) 'whoever, what' before a verb (a del 'whoever may come'; a wnaethost 'what you did') · (6) 3 sg. present of mynet 'goes' (nat a odyno 'that he does not go from there'; yd a hitheu 'she goes'); (7) interrogative particle before a verb (a oes …? 'is there …?'; a dywedy di …? 'will you tell …?'); (8) in a'y kymriw neu archolleu the editorial a'y stands for the conjunction ae 'either' (ae … neu 'either … or'; the Red Book has ae kymriw ae archolleu): read the two halves together as ae · (9) 'as' after an equative (kyn debycket a'r mab 'as like as the boy'; kyn ureisket oed a mab chweblwyd 'as stout as a boy of six')
phawb: pawb (pawb) — everyone; pronoun (a phawb o'r guyrda 'and everyone of the nobles'); spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and'
r: 'r — the article yr contracted after a vowel, apostrophe half of a'r, y'r, o'r etc.: 'the'
e: y — 'his', spelt e before a following consonant or in some spellings: e gwn 'his dogs', e weneb 'his face'; also the preposition 'to' in e uynet 'to go' · also 'her', with h- before a vowel (e hymlit hi 'to pursue her'); the verbal particle y (e deuthum i 'I came'); y of y wrth 'from' (e wrthaw 'from him'); and in e uynyd 'up', e ymdeith 'away' · also the article 'the' (E brenhin, E chwedyl 'the king', 'the news'); 'it' as dummy subject (E doeth im 'it came to me')
guelei: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. imperfect, soft-mutated after y (Llyma y guelei ef 'there he saw')
yn: yn — (1) 'in' (yn Arberth; nasal mutation: yn nyblyc); (2) predicative 'as' with soft mutation (yn wisc hela, yn arglwyd); (3) with a verbal noun, progressive (yn dyuot 'coming'); (4) before an adjective, adverbial (yn llawen 'gladly') · (5) yn yd 'to where' (ymchwelut yn yd oed Pwyll 'returning to where Pwyll was')
uab: mab (mab) — son; noun m., soft-mutated after a personal name in a patronymic (Guawl uab Clut 'Gwawl son of Clud') · also soft after predicative yn (yn uab y wr arall 'a son of another man'; yn uab y Pwyll 'a son of Pwyll')
eurosswyd: Proper name — Euroswydd (ss for s, d for dd), father of Nisien and Efnysien; radical (vowel), after the preposition y 'to'
aeth: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 sg. preterite 'went' (a'y vreic a aeth attaw 'and his wife went to him')
paham: paham (pam) — why?; interrogative adverb, pa + am 'for what'
heb: heb — (1) 'said' (heb ef 'said he'), a defective verb used only for tagging speech; (2) 'without' + verbal noun (heb hanbwyllaw 'without troubling') · (3) 'past, beside' in heb law (heb law yr orssed 'past the mound'); see hebdaw
yr: yr — (1) the article 'the' before a vowel (yr erchwys); (2) 'for, for the sake of' preposition (yr Duw 'for God's sake', yr guaret gormes 'for removing the oppression') · (3) 'for all, however' before an equative-type noun and a clause (yr araued y kerdei y uarch 'for all the slowness with which his horse went'); (4) in yr meityn 'for a while (since)'; (5) the verbal particle y, yd, written yr before a vowel (yr ymordiwedei a hi 'that he would overtake her') · also (6) the perfective particle ry written yr, softening the verb (yr gyscwys 'has slept'); the article before an independent possessive (yr eidunt 'theirs'); 'for' with an abstract noun (yr bychanet 'for the smallness')
na: na — (1) negative particle in a subordinate clause, 'not' (na dywedy di); (2) 'neither/nor' in a series (na guas ystauell, na swydawc) · also negative imperative 'do not', with soft mutation (na ouyn di 'do not ask'; na yrrwch geu arnaf 'do not lay a lie on me'; na hawl ef 'do not claim him')
uy: uy (fy) — my; possessive pronoun, triggers nasal mutation (uy anryded; uy nghyffes; uy gherennyd)
nei: nei (nai) — nephew; noun m. (dy nei ditheu 'your nephew too'); no mutation
chwaer: chwaer (chwaer) — sister; noun f. (dy chwaer 'your sister'; yn chwaer y minheu 'a sister to me'); no mutation (chw- has no mutated form after dy or yn)
i: i — (1) emphatic independent pronoun 'I/me', echoing a verb or conjugated preposition (rof i, arnaf i); (2) spelling of y 'to' before a vowel or l/w (i waret); (3) spelling of y 'his' before some words (i wisc hela 'his hunting-dress') · (4) after ohonawch, probably the 2 pl. echoing pronoun chwi with its ch run into the ending (ohonawch i 'of you')
kyn: kyn (cyn) — before; with a verbal noun (kyn uy rodi 'before my being given') · also the equative particle 'as', softening the adjective (kyn debycket a'r mab 'as like as the boy') · also 'although', with the subjunctive (Kyn ny bwyf arglwydes 'though I am not a lady')
ny: ny (ni/nid) — negative particle 'not', base form before a consonant with soft mutation · also spirant mutation of c, p, t (ny chewch 'you will not get'; ny thygyawd 'it did not avail'); soft mutation of g (ny wybydei 'knew not')
bei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'were, would be' (bei ar y gam 'if it were at its step' = at a walk)
urenhin: brenhin (brenin) — king; noun m., soft-mutated (in apposition or as object): Hafgan urenhin, y deu urenhin · also soft as the predicate complement (a oed urenhin coronawc 'was a crowned king')
ar: ar — (1) preposition 'on, upon; at' (ar Hafgan; ar y carw; ar y gilyd 'against the other'); (2) the article yr after a vowel, 'that which' (noc ar a uu 'than what was'; Ar ny del 'and whoever does not come') · also (3) 'with, accompanied by' (ar y ganuet marchauc 'with his hundred horsemen'); 'in' (ar y ssynnwyr e hun 'in his own senses'; ar perued y digrifwch 'in the middle of the merriment'); ar neill law Pwyll 'on one side of Pwyll'; ar uyrr 'quickly'; ar hynny 'thereupon' (see yny) · also 'over' (ar yr ynys hon 'over this island'); 'after the manner of' (ar ureint kyweirdeb 'in the manner of the arrangement'); 'on' a decision (disgynnu ar gymryt hynny 'settled on taking that'); 'ar ol' 'after' (ar ol Matholwch 'after Matholwch'); ar dec 'on ten' (see dec)
iwerdon: Proper name — Iwerddon (Ireland); noun f.; no mutation (vowel)
da: da — good; adjective, also 'goods, wealth' as a noun (treulaw dy da 'spending your wealth')
oed: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect 'was' (Pwyll... a oed yn arglwyd) · also oed 'appointed time, tryst', noun m., = oet (gwna oed a mi 'make an appointment with me')
genhyf: gan (gan) — with, conjugated 1 sg. 'with me' (eres genhyf 'strange with me'; ryued oed genhyf 'it was a wonder with me'); the gan 'with' of opinion; no mutation
aet: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 sg. imperative 'let him go' (Aet un 'let one go')
llawen: llawen (llawen) — glad, gladly; adjective, base form (yn llawen)
bendigeiduran: Proper name — Bendigeidfran (Bendigeid 'blessed' + bran 'raven, crow'), son of Llŷr, king of the Island of the Mighty; bran is soft-mutated (b>u, u = f) as the second element of the compound; the name itself is unmutated as subject (Bendigeiduran uab Llyr a oed urenhin)
dygaf: dwyn (dwyn) — to bring, carry; 1 sg. present 'I bring' (y dygaf uy nghyffes 'I bring my confession')
uyg: uy (fy) — my; possessive, here spelt uyg before k-: the g is the written trace of the nasal mutation the noun would take (uyg kyuoeth = fy nghyfoeth 'my realm')
kyffes: kyffes (cyffes) — confession; noun f. (ym kyffes y Duw 'by my confession to God'; the Red Book has ym kyffes i y Duw); ym is taken as 'my', and the nasal mutation it brings (nghyffes) is not shown in the spelling
ynteu: ynteu (yntau) — 'he, for his part'; conjunctive pronoun marking a change of speaker or actor (heb ynteu)
uedwl: medwl (meddwl) — mind, thought; noun m., soft-mutated after y 'his' (yn y uedwl) · also soft-mutated (m>u) after pa 'what' (pa uedwl yw yr eidunt 'what intention is theirs')
ys: ys (ys) — 'it is'; copula particle introducing a predicate, esp. in time expressions (ys blwydyn 'it is a year' = for a year) · also the infixed 3 sg. object 's 'it' after pei (pei ys guelwn 'if I saw it') · also 'below, under', is, in the name Wynt Ys Coet 'Gwent Is Coed' · also before the verb in ac aduyd ys kymeraf 'and perhaps I will take' (the Red Book atuyd ys kymeraf): perhaps the particle, perhaps the infixed 's 'it' after aduyd; uncertain
gyflauan: kyflauan (cyflafan) — outrage, atrocity, deed of violence; noun f. (am gyflauan mor anwedus 'for so unseemly an outrage'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the preposition am
wneuthur: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; verbal noun (y wneuthur kynnadeu at Pwyll 'to send envoys to Pwyll', literally 'to make messengers'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the preposition y 'to'
wnaf: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 sg. present/future 'I will do', soft-mutated after a (mi a wnaf hynny) · also 'I will see to it, bring it about that' (mi a wnaf na chaffo ef uiui uyth 'I will see that he never gets me'); auxiliary (Y gymryt a wnaf 'I will take it')
awr: awr (awr) — hour; noun f. (hyt yr awr hon 'until this hour'); no mutation (vowel)
honn: hon (hon) — 'this' (f.); variant spelling of hon (no'r ulwydyn honn 'than this year')
chyuodi: kyuodi (codi) — to rise; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (A chyuodi y uynyd 'and rising up')
uynyd: mynyd (mynydd) — mountain, upward; noun m. used adverbially 'upward', soft-mutated after y (a gyuodes y uynyd 'rose up')
chymryt: kymryt (cymryd) — to take, put on; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chymryt lloppaneu 'and putting on clouts')
chael: caffael (cael) — to get, find; verbal noun (A chael yn y uedwl 'and finding in his mind'); spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and' · also spirant-mutated after no 'than' (no chael iawn 'than getting redress')
dyn: dyn (dyn) — man, person; noun m. (y dyn eithaf 'the farthest man')
ty: ty (tŷ) — house; noun m. (yn y ty yd oed cassec 'in the house was a mare'); no mutation
gauael: gauael (gafael) — a hold, a grip; noun f. (gauael gadarn 'a firm hold')
arnaw: ar — conjugated preposition 'on him, on it' (llithiau dy erchwys dy hun arnaw 'feeding your own pack on it')
yny: yny (hyd oni) — until; so that; conjunction, with a vivid present (yny hyllt, yny dyrr, yny uyd) or the subjunctive for a future goal (yny delych) · also in Ac ar yny llyma, a slip for ar hynny 'thereupon', kept as written (the Red Book has ar hynny) (Ac ar yny, llyma y teulu 'and thereupon, behold the warband')
benn: penn (pen) — head, top, end; noun m.; soft-mutated (p>b) after ar 'on' (ar benn gossed 'on top of a mound'; ar benn y pethewnos 'at the end of the fortnight') · also soft after y 'his' (gauas y benn 'found his head') and after am 'about' (am benn hwnnw 'about that one's head')
welas: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. preterite 'saw', soft-mutated after relative y (yny welas y llys a'r kyuanned)
uranwen: Proper name — Branwen; soft-mutated (b>u) after the preposition gan 'with' (gan Uranwen 'with Branwen') · also soft after ar 'on' (ar Uranwen 'on Branwen') and after y 'to' (y Uranwen 'to Branwen')
tan: tan (tân) — fire; noun m. (y tan a'r glo 'the fire and the charcoal'); no mutation
hi: hi — 'she, her'; independent 3 sg. f. pronoun
uwrw: bwrw (bwrw) — to throw, cast; verbal noun, soft-mutated as possessed object, 'its throwing' = throwing it (yn y uwrw y'r llawr)
neit: neit (naid) — leap, bound; noun f. (ar yr eil neit 'at the second leap')
lle: lle (lle) — place; noun m., base unmutated form
yd: yd — preverbal particle used when the clause opens with an adverb rather than the subject, introducing an indicative main verb (A threigylgweith yd oed yn Arberth)
eisted: eisted (eistedd) — to sit; verbal noun (eisted a wnaethant 'they sat')
rwng: rwng (rhwng) — between; preposition, base uninflected form
deu: deu (dau) — two (m.); numeral, causes soft mutation of a following noun (y deu wrenhin 'the two kings')
uroder: brawt (brawd) — brother; plural broder 'brothers' (modern brodyr); soft-mutated (b>u) after deu 'two' (deu uroder 'two brothers', y deu uroder 'the two brothers')
neill: neill (naill) — one (of two); (o'r neill parth 'on the one side')
law: llaw (llaw) — hand; noun f., soft-mutated after heb in heb law 'past, beside' (heb law yr orssed 'past the mound') · also 'side' in ar neill law 'on one side' (ar neill law Pwyll 'on one side of Pwyll'), soft after neill; 'hand' after possessive 'th (y'th law 'in your hand') · also soft after y 'his' (dodi y law 'putting his hand')
llaw: llaw (llaw) — hand; noun f., in the idiom uch llaw 'above, overlooking' (uch llaw y llys 'above the court') · also gyr llaw 'beside, next to' (eisted gyr llaw hwnnw 'to sit beside it')
arall: arall — other, another; adjective (yr erchwys arall 'the other pack') · also pronoun 'another (woman)' (heb arall 'said another')
hyt: hyt (hyd) — as far as, until; preposition/conjunction (hyt ym penn y ulwydyn 'until the year's end'; hyt na bo 'so that there be not') · also ar hyt 'along' (ar hyt y prifford 'along the highway') · also 'as far as, so far as, as much as, to the extent that' with the subjunctive (hyt y mynnych 'as much as you wish'; hyt y gallwyf y gaffael 'as far as I can get it'); hyt oet y wled 'until the time of the feast' · also 'so that' with the indicative (hyt nat oed rym 'so that there was no use'); hyt yn Aberfraw 'as far as Aberffraw'
llyna: llyna (dyna) — there is, behold that; presentative particle, distal counterpart of llyma
mwyhaf: mawr (mawr) — big, great; superlative mwyaf 'most', spelt mwyhaf (y gwr mwyhaf a gery 'the man you love most')
uu: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. preterite 'was' (bu), soft-mutated after a (tirionwch... a uu y ryngthunt) · also soft-mutated after tra 'while' (tra uu da ganthunt 'while it was good with them')
yniuer: niuer (nifer) — company, host; noun m. with prosthetic y- (yr yniuer y buam doe 'the company that we were yesterday')
un: un (un) — one; numeral/adjective (un dyrnaut 'one blow') · also 'same' (yn un ansawd 'in the same appearance'; yr un ford 'the same way') and the pronoun 'one (of them)' (Un a gyuodes 'one rose')
pawb: pawb (pawb) — everyone; pronoun (pawb a'y dyly 'everyone owes it')
kymryt: kymryt (cymryd) — to take, receive; verbal noun (iawn yw gymryt; kymryt gwrogaeth)
arueu: arueu (arfau) — arms, armour; noun pl. (yny dyrr yr arueu oll 'so that all the armour breaks')
dywot: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 3 sg. preterite 'said' (irregular stem dywot beside dywedwys) (a dywot ef 'and he said')
guern: Proper name — Gwern, son of Matholwch and Branwen (also gwern 'alder'); radical, no mutation (after Sef enw a dodet ar y mab, as predicate)
ym: yn (yn) — in; preposition, spelling variant before p/m/b (hyt ym Penn Llwyn Diarwya; ym perued) · also bot 1 pl. present 'we are' (yd ym y gyt 'we are together'; llibin yd ym pob blwydyn 'wretched that we are every year') · also 'my', a by-form of uy, in the oath ym kyffes y Duw 'by my confession to God' (the Red Book has ym kyffes i y Duw); the nasal mutation it brings is not written
pen: penn (pen) — head, end; noun m., spelling variant with single n (hyt ym pen y ulwydyn)
taryan: taryan (tarian) — shield; noun f. (dyrchauael taryan 'raising a shield', swch y taryan 'the point of the shield'); no mutation (radical, object of the verbal noun)
yscwyd: ysgwydd (ysgwydd) — shoulder; noun f., in the epithet Unic Glew Yscwyd; no mutation (vowel-like, ys-) · also 'shoulder' in ar e yscwyd 'on his shoulder' (e = y 'his'), no mutation
gwydyl: Gwyddel (Gwyddel) — an Irishman; plural Gwydyl 'the Irish'; no mutation after y 'the'
dan: dan (dan) — under; preposition (dan y coet 'under the wood')
peir: peir (pair) — cauldron; noun m. (Mi a rodaf yt peir 'I will give you a cauldron'; y peir 'the cauldron'); no mutation
uei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'might be', soft-mutated after a (a uei uwy no hynny) · also soft-mutated after ban 'when' (ban uei uwyaf 'when it was most')
llawn: llawn (llawn) — full; adjective (a uyd llawn dy got ti uyth 'will your bag ever be full?')
wyr: gwyr (gwŷr) — men; noun pl., soft-mutated after yn (yn wyr ymi 'as men to me') · also soft after o 'of' (o wyr 'of men') and in address (A wyr 'O men') · also soft after y 'to' (y wyr Dyuet 'to the men of Dyfed') and y 'his' (y wyr 'his men')
ymlad: ymlad (ymladd) — to fight; verbal noun (yn herwyd ymlad a frouedigaeth y gorff)
kystal: kystal (cystal) — as good, as much; equative of da 'good' (kystal y doi y gof)
chynt: kynt (cynt) — before, formerly; adverb, spirant-mutated after no (no chynt 'than before')
eithyr: eithyr (eithr) — except; conjunction/preposition (eithyr gadu 'except to leave')
ellynt: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 3 pl. imperfect 'they could' (Ny ellynt wy tremic uwy 'they could not do a greater insult'); the g- is lost by soft mutation after ny (stem ell-)
dywedut: dywedut (dweud) — to say, speak; verbal noun/infinitive
pan: pan (pan) — when; temporal conjunction with a past-time clause (pan doeth) · also interrogative 'from where, whence' (pan doy di? 'where do you come from?')
ynys: ynys (ynys) — island; noun f. (yr ynys hon 'this island'); no mutation
kedyrn: cadarn (cadarn) — strong, mighty; plural kedyrn (cedyrn) used as a noun, 'the mighty', in Ynys y Kedyrn 'the Island of the Mighty'; no mutation after the article
ef: ef (ef) — 'he, him'; independent 3 sg. m. pronoun
ui: ui (fi) — me; object pronoun after an imperative (dygwch ui odyma 'carry me from here') · also the softened pronoun 'I' after a verb (Ny allaf ui arnaf a dywedy di uyth 'I cannot bring myself to do what you say') and as the second, emphatic pronoun in mi ui 'I myself' (A mi ui a rodaf 'and I myself will give'); soft-mutated from mi
mot: bot (bod) — to be; verbal noun, nasal-mutated (b>m) after the possessive uy 'my' (uy mot y ueichawc 'my being pregnant')
achaws: achaws (achos) — cause, reason; noun m. ('Pa achaws' 'what reason, why')
meuyl: meuyl (mefl) — shame, disgrace; noun m., used in the oath meuyl im 'shame on me'
ymi: y (i) + mi — conjugated preposition 'to me' (pa gyuarwyd a uyd ymi)
ony: ony (oni) — unless, until; conjunction ('no, unless …'), causes spirant mutation of c, p, t (ony chyuyt 'unless there rise') · also with soft mutation of g (ony wybydaf i 'if I do not find out')
waret: gwaret (gwared) — to remove, take off; verbal noun, soft-mutated after i 'to' (i waret i wisc hela)
rac: rac (rhag) — before, lest, to prevent, for fear of; preposition (dyro ui idaw rac anglot yt 'give me to him to spare you dishonour')
hynn: hynn (hyn) — 'this'; demonstrative, substantive use in ual hynn 'like this, thus' · also adjective 'this' after its noun (seith cantref hynn 'these seven cantrefs')
dyuot: dyuot (dyfod) — to come; verbal noun (a dyuot y Lynn Cuch 'and coming to Glyn Cuch')
idaw: idaw (iddo) — to him; 3 sg. m. conjugated form of y 'to'
rith: rith (rhith) — shape, form, guise; noun m. (byd di i'm rith yno 'be there in my shape')
gwydel: Gwyddel (Gwyddel) — an Irishman; noun m. sg. (y Gwydel 'the Irishman'); no mutation
dyrr: torri (torri) — to break; 3 sg. present, vivid narrative tense 'breaks' (yny dyrr yr arueu oll 'so that all the armour breaks')
hynny: hynny — 'that (thing)'; demonstrative pronoun, very frequent (a hynny 'and that')
bu: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. preterite 'was' (a uu 'was'; Llawen uu 'glad was')
seithwyr: seithwyr (saith gŵr) — seven men, a company of seven; seith + gwyr (adaw seithwyr 'to leave seven men'); modern has saith gŵr
sef: sef (sef) — it is (this), that is; presentative particle introducing an explanation or answer
pryderi: Pryderi (Pryderi) — proper name, the son of Pwyll and Rhiannon, named from pryder 'care'; no mutation
manawydan: Proper name — Manawydan, son of Llŷr, brother of Bendigeidfran; radical (subject, after a 'and')
eil: eil (ail) — second; ordinal numeral (yr eil 'the second')
hen: hen (hen) — old; adjective, as an epithet after a name (Heueyd Hen 'Hefeydd the Old')
peris: peri (peri) — to cause, command; 3 sg. preterite 'he caused' (y peris ef dyuot 'he had come'); radical after the particle y
llad: llad (lladd) — to kill; verbal noun, base form (y'm llad i 'to kill me') · also llad glwm 'to tie a knot' (idiomatic, literally 'strike a knot'): llad glwm ar garryeu y got 'to tie a knot on the straps of the bag'
chwi: chwi (chi) — 'you' (pl.); pronoun (y'ch kynnal chwi 'to maintain you')
penn: penn (pen) — head, end; noun m., base form (Penn Annwuyn 'Head of Annwfn')
dygwch: dwyn (dwyn) — to carry; 2 pl. imperative 'carry!' (dygwch ui odyma 'carry me from here')
wyneb: gwyneb (wyneb) — face; noun m., base unmutated form
ford: ford (ffordd) — road, way; noun f., f written for ff (y'r ford 'to the road'; yr un ford 'the same way')
hir: hir (hir) — long; adjective (yn hir 'for a long time')
hardlech: Proper name — Harlech (hardd 'fair' + llech 'slab, rock'), the court in Ardudwy; no mutation (h- is not mutated after yn 'in')
bydwch: bot (bod) — to be; 2 pl. imperative 'be' (A bydwch gedymdeithon chwitheu 'and be companions, you also'), -wch; no mutation
mlyned: blwydyn (blwyddyn) — year; plural blyned (modern blynedd), spelt mlyned (hyt ym penn y seith mlyned 'until the end of the seven years'); nasal-mutated (b>m) after seith 'seven'
riannon: Riannon (Rhiannon) — proper name, daughter of Heueyd Hen
canu: canu (canu) — to sing, sound (a horn); verbal noun (canu y gorn 'sounding his horn')
ywch: y (i) + chwi — 'to you'; conjugated preposition, 2 pl. (rodo da ywch 'may he give good to you'); no mutation
uyd: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. present/future 'is, will be' (byd), soft-mutated after a or a predicate (Dilesteir uyd dy hynt; yny uyd Hafgan)
gedymdeithas: kedymdeithas (cydymdeithas) — fellowship, companionship; noun f., soft-mutated after y (kedymdeithas y ryngthunt 'fellowship between them')
oreu: goreu (gorau) — best; superlative of da 'good', softened after a feminine noun (y neges oreu 'the best errand') · also soft as predicate after bu (yn gystal ac y bu oreu 'as good as he was best')
ban: pan (pan) — when; conjunction, spelt ban here (ban uydynt, ban uei 'when they were, when it was'); the b is a spelling of the conjunction, followed by a soft-mutated verb · also hyt ban 'until' (hyt ban gauas y benn 'until he found his head'; o hyn hyt ban del amgen 'from now until something else comes')
arnaf: ar — conjugated preposition 'on me' (arnaf i 'on me')
eiryoet: eiryoet (erioed) — ever; variant spelling of eiroet (o'r a welsei eiryoet 'of all he had ever seen')
drws: drws (drws) — door; noun m. (y drws 'the door'); no mutation
parth: parth (parth) — towards, side, direction; noun m./preposition (parth a'y lys 'towards his court')
uot: bot (bod) — to be; verbal noun, soft-mutated after a (ef a eill uot yn ediuar gennyf) · also soft as the complement of a verb (a dylyei uot 'that ought to be')
yno: yno (yno) — there; adverb (ac yno y bu y nos honno)
genhwch: gan (gan) — with; conjugated preposition 2 pl. 'with you' (a chwedleu genhwch 'and have you tidings')
lundein: Proper name — Llundein (Llundain), London; soft-mutated (ll>l) after the feminine noun coron 'crown' (goron Lundein 'the crown of London')
drwod: drwod (drosodd) — across, over; adverb (y doeth ef drwod attat ti 'he came across to you'); no mutation
kychwynassant: kychwyn (cychwyn) — to set out, start; 3 pl. preterite in -assant 'they set out' (Ac y kychwynassant 'and they set out'); no mutation after the particle y
branwen: Proper name — Branwen, daughter of Llŷr; radical (object of erchi 'to ask for')
tal: tal (tal) — payment; noun m., first element of the name Tal Ebolyon (Talebolion, 'payment of colts'); also tal 'front, end', so the name may have meant something else; no mutation (radical)
ebolyon: ebawl (ebol) — foal; noun m., plural ebolyon (yr ebolyon 'the foals'); no mutation
doethant: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 pl. preterite 'they came' (Y'r llys y doethant 'to the court they came')
tir: tir (tir) — land, territory; noun m. (dylyedauc tir a dayar 'a lord of land and earth')
wnaethant: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 pl. preterite 'they did', soft-mutated after a (eisted a wnaethant)
edrych: edrych (edrych) — to look; verbal noun (edrych ar y carw 'to look at the stag')
oheni: o + hi — conjugated preposition 'from her/it' (yd hanwyf oheni 'that I come from it')
hitheu: hitheu (hithau) — conjunctive form of hi 'she', 'she for her part'
welei: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. imperfect 'he saw' (welei), soft-mutated after a (ef a welei lannerch) · also 'would see' (neu ynteu a welei rywedawt 'or else he would see a wonder')
ohonunt: o (o) + wynt — 'of them, from them'; conjugated preposition, 3 pl. (kyscu a wnaeth pawb ohonunt 'every one of them slept'); no mutation
ni: ni — (1) 1 pl. pronoun 'we/us' (yd ymdidanyssam ni); (2) negative particle, spelling variant of ny before some verbs (ni ladaf, ni bu)
m: 'm — infixed/proclitic pronoun, apostrophe half of a'm, y'm, o'm etc.: 'my' (possessive, triggers soft mutation) or 'me' (object) · with h- before a following vowel (o'm hanwod 'against my will'); as 'my' before a verbal noun it may stand for that noun's object (a'm rodi 'and my giving' = and giving me); as 'me' after a relative (a'm gwrthyt 'who rejects me')
dwy: dwy (dwy) — two (f.); numeral, causes soft mutation of a following feminine noun (y dwy dyrnas 'the two kingdoms')
dodi: dodi (dodi) — to put; verbal noun (dodi y deudroet yn y got 'to put his two feet in the bag'; dodi llef ar y gorn 'to give a blast on the horn')
uawr: mawr (mawr) — great, big; adjective (grauanc uawr 'a great claw'); soft-mutated (m>u) after a feminine noun · also predicative, soft-mutated directly after the verb (nyt oed uawr y weilgi 'the sea was not great')
thorri: torri (torri) — to cut, break, cut off; verbal noun (a thorri y guefleu 'and cutting the lips'); spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'and'
gwneuthur: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; verbal noun/infinitive, also used as the periphrastic auxiliary 'do' (a wneuthum itt 'that I did to you')
idi: idi (iddi) — to her; 3 sg. f. conjugated form of y 'to' (menegi... a wnaeth idi)
kerdet: kerdet (cerdded) — going, walking; verbal noun, also a noun 'pace, gait' (kerdet araf guastat 'a slow, even pace'; o'r kerdet mwyaf 'to the greatest pace')
wnaeth: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. preterite 'he did', soft-mutated after a; auxiliary in 'verbal noun + a wnaeth' (dechreu ymdidan a wnaeth)
ganthunt: gan — conjugated preposition 'with them' (ni bu newydach ganthunt 'it was no more novel to them')
val: ual (fel) — as; conjunction, spelt val (Ac val y bydynt 'and as they were')
llyma: llyma (dyma) — behold, here is; presentative particle throwing a scene before the reader (llyma yr erchwys)
wynt: wynt (hwynt) — they, them; 3 pl. pronoun (un lliw ac wynt 'the same colour as them') · also Wynt, Gwent, in the name Wynt Ys Coet 'Gwent Is Coed', a region of south-east Wales
gwraged: gwreic (gwraig) — woman, wife; noun f., plural gwraged (modern gwragedd) (a gwraged 'and women'; gwyr a gwraged 'men and women')
oes: bot (bod) — to be; present 3 sg. existential 'there is' (Nit oes yndi nep)
chwedleu: chwedl (chwedl) — tale, story, talk; noun f., plural chwedleu (y chwedleu ereill 'the other tales'); ch- does not mutate here
nac: nac — (1) negative used in a direct answer, repeating the verb, 'no' (Nac attygaf 'I will not'); (2) 'nor' before a vowel (nac ymdidan) · also negative imperative 'do not' (nac arch dim 'do not ask anything')
onyt: onyt (onid) — unless; conjunction (onyt ti a'm gwrthyt 'unless (it be) you (who) reject me')
coronawc: coronawc (coronog) — crowned; adjective from coron 'crown' + -awc (urenhin coronawc 'a crowned king'); no mutation (follows its noun)
pa: pa (pa) — what, which; interrogative adjective, triggers soft mutation of the following noun
daruu: daruot (darfod) — to finish, be finished; 3 sg. preterite 'was finished', with y/i of the person (pan daruu udunt y bwyd 'when they had finished the meal')
wynteu: wynt (hwynt) — they, for their part; conjunctive 3 pl. pronoun (Wynteu hagen ni wybuyssynt)
bran: Proper name — Bran (Bendigeidfran), father of Caradog; radical, no mutation (after uab: patronymic leaves the father's name unmutated)
edewit: edewit (addewid) — promise; noun (dy edewit 'your promise') · also impersonal preterite of adaw 'to leave': 'was left' (yd edewit y gwyr hynny 'those men were left')
gyt: kyt (cyd) — together; in y gyt (a) 'together (with)' (y gyt ac wynt 'together with them')
am: am — preposition 'about, around; concerning' (am y uynwgyl 'about his neck'; am dir a dayar 'about land') · also 'for, in return for' (am y gam 'for his wrong'; am pob un 'for each one')
ohonaw: o + ef — conjugated preposition 'of/by him' (edrych ohonaw ef 'his looking')
welet: gwelet (gweld) — to see; verbal noun, soft-mutated after dy 'your' (dy welet ti 'seeing you', literally 'your seeing') · also soft after o 'from, because of' (o welet gwr kymeint a gerynt 'from seeing a man so loved by them')
cledyf: cledyf (cleddyf) — sword; noun m. (tynnu cledyf 'to draw a sword'); no mutation (object of a verbal noun)
pwy: pwy (pwy) — who; interrogative pronoun (pwy wyt ti 'who are you')
lladei: llad (lladd) — to strike, kill; 3 sg. imperfect 'would strike, used to strike' (y lladei ef y march 'he would strike the horse')
wiscaw: gwiscaw (gwisgo) — to dress, clothe; verbal noun, soft-mutated after y 'to' (y wiscaw eurwisc) · also soft after an object of erchi (erchwch y wyr y llys wiscaw amdanunt 'bid the men of the court put on gear about them')
llen: llen (llen) — cloth, mantle, covering; noun f. (Llen o bali 'a cloth of brocade'); no mutation
hut: hut (hud) — magic, illusion, enchantment; noun m. (ystyr hut 'a meaning of magic')
amdanaw: am — conjugated preposition 'about him' (3 sg. m.); clothing/objects are 'about' a person (gwisc ... amdanaw)
neb: neb (neb) — anyone; pronoun, used with a positive sense in relative/superlative clauses (o'r a welsei neb 'that anyone had seen') · also 'anyone' under a negative = 'no one' (ny thykya y neb ymlit 'it avails no one to pursue') · also in y neb a 'the one who/to whom' (y neb a dylyer y kymryt y ganthaw 'the one from whom one ought to take it')
gwyr: gwr (gŵr) — men; noun pl. (kymryt gwrogaeth y gwyr 'taking the homage of the men') · also gwyr 3 sg. present of gwybot 'knows' (onys gwyr Branwen 'unless Branwen knows it')
namyn: namyn (namyn) — except, but; conjunction (namyn ti 'but you')
lad: lladd (lladd) — to kill; verbal noun (am lad o honaf uu hun uy mab 'for my killing of my own son'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after the preposition am · also soft-mutated (ll>l) after the possessive 'e 'his' (na'e lad 'nor his killing')
trydyd: trydyd (trydydd) — third; ordinal (ar y trydyd 'at the third')
dyuet: Dyuet (Dyfed) — proper name, the region of south-west Wales
was: gwas (gwas) — lad, servant; noun m., soft-mutated in address (Ha was 'ho, lad'; Bid parawt … was 'be ready, lad') and after wrth (wrth was y uarch 'to his groom', literally 'the lad of his horse') · also soft after predicative yn (yn was ieuanc 'as a young lad')
coet: coet (coed) — wood, forest; noun m. (dan y coet 'under the wood')
dechreussant: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; 3 pl. preterite in -ssant 'they began' (A'r gyuedach a dechreussant 'and the carousing they began'); no mutation shown after the relative a (the soft mutation of d- is not written)
dechreuwyt: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; impersonal preterite 'was begun' in -wyt (y dechreuwyt kymyscu y tan 'the mixing of the fire was begun'); no mutation after the particle y
uwyt: bwyt (bwyd) — food; noun m., soft-mutated after o (diwallaf o uwyt a llynn 'best supplied with food and drink')
llynn: llynn (llyn) — drink; noun m. (bwyt a llynn 'food and drink') · also llyn 'lake, pool' (llynn o pop parth y'r eskeir 'a lake on each side of the ridge')
dechreuyssant: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they began' (ual y dechreuyssant eisted 'as they began to sit'); no mutation after the particle y
uwyta: bwyta (bwyta) — to eat; verbal noun, soft-mutated after y 'to' (mynet y uwyta 'go to eat')
ederyn: ederyn (aderyn) — bird; noun m.; object of the verbal noun meithryn, no mutation (vowel)
dechreu: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; verbal noun (dechreu dygyuor 'beginning to muster') · also the noun 'beginning' (ar dechreu kyuedach 'at the start of the carousing')
udunt: y (i) + wynt — conjugated preposition 'to them' (Amser a doeth udunt e uynet e gyscu)
ryw: ryw (rhyw) — some, some kind of; before its noun (ryw ystyr hut 'some meaning of magic') · also y ryw wr 'what kind of man'; ryw 'sort, kind' as a noun
gerd: kerd (cerdd) — art, music, song; noun f.; soft-mutated (c>g) after o 'of' (o gerd arwest 'of the art of music')
oc: o (o) — 'of, from', spelt oc before a vowel (oc eu hanuod 'against their will'); no mutation
diuwyn: diuwyn — worthless, unpleasing (which shade is meant is debated); adjective, di- 'without' + mwyn 'pleasing, worth', softened (bot yn diuwyn ganthaw 'that it was worthless in his eyes')
pob: pob (pob) — each, every; adjective (pob un 'each one')
dremynt: tremynt (no modern form; cf. trem 'look') — a sight, spectacle; noun m.; written softened (t>d) with no visible cause: Evans prints no e 'the' before it (the second witness's e dremynt would explain it) (o achaws dremynt 'because of a sight')
guelet: gwelet (gweld) — to see; verbal noun, gu for gw (A guelet a wnaeth 'and he saw')
uch: uch (uwch) — above, over; preposition (uch llaw y llys 'above the court') · also 'high' as adjective/adverb, comparative in yn uch no bwrd y llong 'higher than the ship's board'
weilgi: gweilgi (gweilgi) — the open sea, the main (a poetic word); noun f.; soft-mutated (gw>w) after the feminine article y (uch penn y weilgi 'above the head of the sea')
allan: allan — out, forth; adverb ('o hynny allan' 'from then on')
chyn: kyn (cyn) — although, though; spirant-mutated after a (a chyn nyt ymdialwyf 'and though I do not avenge myself') · also the equative particle cyn 'as', spirant-mutated after a 'and' (a chyn ureisket oed a mab chweblwyd 'and as stout as a boy of six') · also 'before' (a chyn penn y pedwyryd mis 'and before the end of the fourth month')
wy: wynt (hwynt) — they; 3 pl. pronoun, spelling variant (heb wy 'said they')
bydynt: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. habitual imperfect 'they were (being), they used to be', beside oedynt (ual y bydynt yn eisted 'as they were sitting')
buant: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. preterite 'they were' (Ny buant 'they were not')
ulwydyn: blwydyn (blwyddyn) — year; noun f., soft-mutated after y/the feminine article (hyt ym penn y ulwydyn) · also adverbial, 'a year' in time phrases, soft-mutated without the article (ulwydyn y heno 'a year from tonight'; ual yd eistedyssant ulwydyn o'r nos honno 'as they sat a year from that night'), the soft mutation being that of an adverbial accusative of time
yneuad: neuad (neuadd) — hall; noun f., spelt with prothetic y- (Y'r yneuad yd aethont 'into the hall they went'); no mutation
neuad: neuad (neuadd) — hall; noun f. (y'r neuad y gyrchwys)
welynt: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 pl. imperfect 'they saw', soft-mutated after a (wynt a welynt 'they saw'; yny welynt 'until they saw')
agoret: agoret (agored) — open; adjective, past participle in -et (yn agoret 'open'); no mutation (vowel)
racco: racco (acw) — yonder; adverb after a noun (yr unbennes racco 'the lady yonder')
agori: agori (agor) — to open; verbal noun (Agori y drws a oruc ef 'he opened the door'); no mutation
nos: nos (nos) — night; noun f. (y nos honno 'that night')
diwall: diwall (diwall) — without want, provided, abundant; adjective (yn diwall o uwyt a llyn 'abundantly of food and drink'); no mutation shown after yn (the soft form ddiwall is not written)
digrif: digrif (digri) — pleasant, amusing; adjective (y bu digrif ganthaw 'it was pleasant to him')
welsynt: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 pl. pluperfect 'they had seen' in -synt (na welsynt eiryoet 'that they had never seen'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the negative na
gwyd: gwyd (gŵydd) — presence, sight; noun m., in the phrase yg gwyd 'in the presence of' (yg gwyd gwyrda 'in the presence of noblemen'), with the nasal mutation after yn written yg gwyd
hun: hun (hun) — self, own; also 'sleep' as a separate noun by context (e hunan/e hun 'himself'; kymryt hun 'to take sleep')
doy: dyuot (dod) — to come; 2 sg. present 'you come' (pan doy di 'where do you come from?')
gof: cof (cof) — memory, mind; noun m., soft-mutated after y (y gof 'to mind')
dim: dim — anything, nothing; indefinite pronoun (ny russya dim ragot 'nothing will obstruct before you')
byt: byt (byd) — world; noun m. (o helgwn y byt 'of the hunting dogs of the world')
treulyssant: treulio (treulio) — to spend, pass (time); 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they spent' (Uelly y treulyssant blwydyn a blwydyned 'so they spent a year and years'); no mutation after the particle y
dwyn: dwyn (dwyn) — to carry, bring; verbal noun (dwyn y dwy dyrnas yn un 'bringing the two kingdoms into one')
no: no (na) — than, comparative particle (no gyrru 'than driving'; no chyuedach)
nyt: ny (nid) — negative particle 'not, it is not', spelling before a vowel or in emphasis (nyt teilygdawt)
adnabot: adnabot (adnabod) — to know, recognise; verbal noun (adnabot meithryn yr ederyn 'recognising the nursing of the bird')
gilyd: kilid (cilydd) — 'the other, fellow'; variant spelling of gilid (ar y gilyd 'against the other')
amser: amser — time; noun m. (Amser a doeth udunt 'the time came to them')
nit: nyt (nid) — negative particle 'not, there is not', spelling before a vowel (Nit oes; Nit yttoydwn)
phan: pan (pan) — when; spirant-mutated after a 'and' (A phan doeth yno)
uuassei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had been' (buassei), soft-mutated after a (beth a uuassei y arglwydiaeth ef)
gelwit: galw (galw) — to call; 3 sg. impersonal imperfect 'he was called' (y gelwit Pwyll Penn Annwuyn)
matholwch: Proper name — Matholwch, king of Ireland; radical, no mutation (subject or in apposition: mae ymma Matholwch brenhin Iwerdon)
dydgueith: dydgueith (no modern form) — one day, on a day; dyd 'day' + gweith 'time', adverbial (Ac ar hynny dydgueith 'and at that, one day'); no mutation
wybot: gwybot (gwybod) — knowledge, discernment; noun m. used substantively (ny bu gystal dy wybot 'your judgement was never so good') · also the verbal noun 'to know, find out', soft-mutated after y 'to' (y wybot pwy yw 'to find out who she is')
ay: ay (ai) — is it?; interrogative particle (Ay uelly y mynny di 'is it so you wish?') · also ay … ay 'whether … or, either … or' (ay yma ay yn Ynys y Kedyrn 'whether here or in the Island of the Mighty')
gwir: gwir (gwir) — true, truth; adjective/noun m. (pei gwir hynny 'if that were true'); no mutation
gyn: kyn (cyn) — as, equative particle before an adjective (kyn hygaret 'as lovable', spelt gyn after ny) · also soft-mutated in a run of epithets after the feminine noun morwyn (morwyn gystal, kyuurd, gyn anwylet 'a maiden so good, of equal rank, so dear')
drwc: drwc (drwg) — evil, harm, wrong; noun m. (ny chewch un drwc 'you will get no harm'); no mutation
chyt: kyt (cyd) — although; spirant-mutated after a (a chyt archo ef 'and though he ask')
benhaf: pennaf (pennaf) — chief, foremost; superlative formed from penn 'head'; soft-mutated (p>b) after y 'as' (a Chradawc uab Bran y benhaf 'and Caradog son of Brân as chief') and after predicative yn (yn benhaf kynweisyat 'as chiefest steward')
oll: oll (oll) — all, wholly; adverb/adjective intensifying a preceding noun (yr arueu oll 'all the armour')
harglwyd: arglwyd (arglwydd) — lord; noun m. (a'e harglwyd 'and their lord'); h- prefixed to the vowel after the possessive e/eu 'their'
bynnac: bynnac (bynnag) — -ever, indefinite particle after peth/pwy etc.; 'Peth bynnac' 'whatever'
pann: pan (pan) — when; temporal conjunction, spelt pann (Pann doethont 'when they came'); causes soft mutation, not shown on d- (dd)
cany: cany — 'since … not'; conjunction can 'since' + the negative ny, softening the verb (Cany welas ef 'since he did not see')
doey: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 sg. imperfect 'used to come, would come' (Ny doey wr mawr 'no great man would come'); the soft mutation of wr after it is the subject following the verb
byth: byth (byth) — ever, for ever; adverb (Nyt byth y perhey di 'you will not last for ever'); no mutation
drwy: trwy (trwy) — through; preposition, soft-mutated form (drwy y dewred ef 'through his valour')
tra: tra (tra) — while; conjunction (tra deweis wrthyt ti 'while I kept silent') · also (2) 'very', before an adjective with spirant mutation (tra chyuoethauc 'very mighty'); (3) 'while' with the verb sometimes soft-mutated (tra barhaud)
dyweit: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 3 sg. present 'says' (guir a dyweit 'he tells the truth'); modern dywed
yw: bot (bod) — to be; present 3 sg. copula 'is', used in equative sentences (Sef yw hwnnw, Hafgan)
byw: byw — alive; adjective (ny byd byw ef 'he will not be alive')
mywn: y mywn (i mewn) — in, inside; adverbial phrase (yn dyuot y mywn 'coming in')
wraged: gwreic (gwraig) — woman, wife; noun f., plural gwraged, soft-mutated after holl 'all' (holl wraged 'all the women') · also soft after o 'of' (riuedi o wraged 'a number of women') and in address (A wraged 'O women')
anet: geni (geni) — to be born; impersonal preterite 'was born' (mab a anet idaw 'a son was born to him'); soft-mutated (g>∅) after the relative a
weisson: gwas (gwas) — lad, servant, groom; noun m., plural gweisson (y weisson y meirych 'to the grooms of the horses'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the preposition y 'to' (and after at)
mawr: mawr (mawr) — big, great; adjective (uarch erchlas mawr 'a big dapple-grey horse')
uedylyssant: medylyaw (meddylio) — to think, consider; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they thought' (Sef kynghor a uedylyssant 'the counsel they thought'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the relative a
gantunt: gan (gan) — with; conjugated preposition 3 pl. 'with them' (a'r gennadwri honno gantunt 'with that message with them')
kyscu: kyscu (cysgu) — to sleep; verbal noun, base form (yd wyt yn kyscu heno 'you are to sleep tonight')
uam: mam (mam) — mother; noun f. (y mab a'y uam 'the boy and his mother'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the possessive y 'his' · also soft-mutated (m>u) after un 'one' (un uam ac ef 'of one mother with him') and after the possessive 'e (o'e uam 'by his mother')
gilid: kilid (cilydd) — 'the other, fellow'; used in y gilid 'to the other', wrth y gilid 'towards the other'
gwledychu: gwledychu (gwladychu) — to rule, reign; verbal noun (gwledychu o honaw 'his ruling')
wlat: gwlat (gwlad) — land, country; noun f., soft-mutated after the feminine article or possessive (y wlat; i'th wlat)
rannu: rannu (rhannu) — to share, divide, allot; verbal noun (Ac eu rannu a wnaethant 'and they divided them'); r- for rh-; no mutation
rydunt: y rwng (rhwng) — between; conjugated 3 pl. 'between them' (y bu duundeb y rydunt 'there was concord between them')
gelwir: galw (galw) — to call, name; impersonal present 'is called' (Ac y gelwir y rei hynny 'and those are called'), -ir, a>e by affection; no mutation after the particle y
rann: rann (rhan) — part; noun f. (y rann a dylyei uot 'the part that ought to be')
buassei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had been' (megys y buassei y mab 'how the boy had been'), -ssei; no mutation after the particle y
aryant: aryant (arian) — silver, money; noun m. (llathen aryant 'a rod of silver'); no mutation (vowel)
ual: ual (fel) — as, like; conjunction/preposition (ual hynn 'like this') · also 'so that' (ual yd ymglywynt 'so that they could hear one another'; ual y bydynt gadarnach 'so that they would be stronger') and 'how' (sef ual yd eistedyssant 'that is how they sat')
teruyna: terfynu (terfynu) — to end, finish; 3 sg. present 'ends' (y teruyna y geing hon yma 'this branch ends here'); no mutation after the particle y
geing: keing (cainc) — branch, strand, a branch of the Mabinogi; noun f. (y geing hon 'this branch'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the feminine article y
tryded: trydyd (trydydd) — third; ordinal, feminine form tryded (trydedd) (A honno oed tryded prif rieni 'and she was the third chief ...'); no mutation (soft mutation after predicative yn is not written: yn tryded)
pedeir: pedeir (pedair) — four (f.); numeral, in pedeir degwlat 'four ten-lands'
seithugeint: seithugeint (saith ugain) — seven score, 140; numeral (seith 'seven' + ugeint 'twenty')
dial: dial (dial) — vengeance, revenge; noun m. (na dial uyth 'nor vengeance ever')
